title: Episode 11 trains nothing, so it inherits Episode 10's training health verbatim, including its one failing check. These checks are about whether the FRAGILITY MEASUREMENT is sound, not whether the policy is.

checks.name: perturbation_changes_the_outcome
checks.detail: across the 4 designs that complete the lap unperturbed, mean failure rate 0% -> 4% once perturbed. Measured on those designs only: a car that already fails 100% of the time fails 100% under perturbation too, and averaging it in hides whether the disturbance does anything at all.
checks.group: Is the perturbation actually perturbing anything?

checks.name: perturbation_does_not_saturate
checks.detail: at least one design survives and at least one does not. A level where everything fails ranks nothing, and neither does one where everything survives — both would produce a flat Pareto front that looks like a finding.
checks.group: Is the perturbation actually perturbing anything?

checks.name: some_designs_are_statistically_distinguishable
checks.detail: 4 of 10 design pairs have disjoint 95% Wilson intervals on the perturbed finish rate at n = 40. With overlapping intervals everywhere the ranking would be decoration.
checks.group: Can the differences between designs be believed?

checks.name: most_laps_are_inside_the_fit
checks.detail: the leanest quotable cell keeps 85% of its laps inside the +/-12 deg fit, and the highest median worst-slip across them is 7.8 deg. Laps that excurse are discarded individually rather than disqualifying their whole condition (rule 4 is a per-lap rule).
checks.group: Is enough of the data inside the tire model to use?

checks.name: discarded_failures_are_declared
checks.detail: 9 of 25 quotable cells discarded at least one lap that BOTH failed and left the fit. For those cells the in-fit failure rate is a LOWER BOUND — the discarded crashes are real crashes we cannot attribute to the car rather than to our extrapolation. This check always passes; it exists to put the number in the report.
checks.group: Is enough of the data inside the tire model to use?

checks.name: the_beyond_condition_really_is_beyond
checks.detail: the `beyond` condition reaches 28.6 deg of slip. It is reported and excluded from every claim. This check exists so the exclusion is justified by measurement rather than by assertion — if `beyond` turned out to stay inside the fit, it would be quotable and the episode's conclusion would change.
checks.group: Is enough of the data inside the tire model to use?

checks.name: a_speed_fragility_tradeoff_is_measurable_inside_the_fit
checks.detail: the worst in-fit failure rate on a drivable car is 8%. At 0% there would be no fragility to rank and the Pareto front this episode set out to measure would not exist at any defensible disturbance. An earlier 10-rollout calibration said exactly that and was wrong — see FINDINGS F70.
checks.group: Is there any disturbance that breaks it inside the fit?

checks.name: the_faster_car_is_the_more_fragile_one
checks.detail: in-fit failure rate falls monotonically as the cars get slower: 0.47 8% -> 0.54 0% -> 0.61 0% -> 0.65 0%. This is the episode's claim; if the ordering were scrambled there would be a tradeoff in magnitude but not one you could act on.
checks.group: Is there any disturbance that breaks it inside the fit?
